decode_refusals.note: an enablement this build does not define fails closed rather than decoding to a default a client would act on — and the safe-looking guess for an unnameable state is the wrong one
a refusal word outside the eight this build carries; the vocabulary is closed on both sides of the wire
a durable identity starts at one; zero names a row no writer produced
a negative identity is a malformed body rather than an unwritten row: the decoder converts before it judges the domain, and the two categories differ

registration writes revision one and every accepted transition writes one higher, so zero is a row no writer produced — a different statement from an unwritten row identity, under a different category
the same rule on a receipt, which is the answer a write returns
a registration instant the store's own `created_at_ms >= 0` constraint cannot hold
the same constraint on the instant a write reports

an empty cause is refused rather than read as `no reason given`: a withdrawal an operator cannot safely resume from is the one this product does not offer a spelling for. The absence of a cause is null
the field is a string or a null and nothing else; a number is a malformed body rather than a cause
one byte over the identity bound, measured in UTF-8 bytes rather than in the UTF-16 code units a JavaScript `length` counts
an empty actor names nobody, and this lane records who asked
a schedule that is prose rather than a canonical rendering: the wire carries `once@<ms>` and `every@<ms>` and nothing an operator typed
`every@0` would fire without advancing; the interval is strictly positive on both sides of the wire
an empty scope serializes under nothing; the absence of a scope is null, and only beside a null schedule
an instant the registry's `next_fire_at_ms >= 0` constraint cannot hold
an execution instant is an integer or a null and nothing else
an empty prompt is a job that submits nothing; the absence of a prompt is null, and only beside a null schedule
the prompt member is a string or a null and nothing else
a detail body is a record plus its prompt; a record on its own is a body of the wrong shape, however well-formed the record
one row past MAX_AUTOMATION_PAGE_ITEMS. The length is judged before any item is read, so what these items are does not matter and the refusal names the length
a cursor below the beginning of the listing
the wire carries true or false for a continuation and nothing else
a conflict about a revision no writer produced tells a caller to retry against nothing
an unexpected key is refused rather than ignored
a missing key is refused rather than defaulted, inside a nested body as much as at the top level
the prompt travels on a detail read and never in a listing; a page item carrying one is a record of the wrong shape
a kind this protocol version does not define, which is a different answer from a kind it defines and this surface does not decode
the Runs lane's name on this lane's decoder, refused on the name axis so each protocol's closed kind set stays closed
this protocol at a major version neither side implements
a payload that parses but is not canonical is refused, not normalized
zero bytes is not an empty message

encode_refusals.note: the coupling, on the way out: a pause with no stated cause is refused before a frame is spent, because a withdrawal an operator cannot safely resume from is not a request this product has a shape for
the terminal state owes a cause as much as the resumable one does
the other half of the coupling: a resume that states a cause is refused rather than silently dropping the cause, which would leave the caller believing it recorded something
zero names a row no writer produced, which is a different fault from a counter the wire cannot carry — and the two categories differ
one past the largest integer this wire carries: the same branded constructor refuses it, and the encoder reports the other end of the range

a brand exists only in the type checker, so the builder is where an untyped caller's undefined state is stopped. The coupling passes first — an unknown target requires no cause and none is given — so what refuses this is the vocabulary rather than the relation
one byte over the cause bound, measured in UTF-8 bytes
one byte over the identity bound, which the registry grammar itself refuses before the narrower scheduled bound is reached

one byte over the scheduled identity bound: an identity the registry could hold but whose occurrence key could never fit the durable submit lane, refused before a frame is spent rather than registered and never fired
a control character in an actor, which the wire never carries raw
an empty prompt is a job that submits nothing
one byte over the prompt bound, which is the durable submit lane's task bound
a scope is an identifier, not prose: the newline a prompt may carry is outside a scope's grammar

a schedule that is prose rather than a canonical rendering, stopped where an untyped caller reaches the builder: what an operator typed is parsed into a rendering before it reaches the wire, never carried as typed
an empty identity names nothing
a page that admits nothing cannot make progress, so zero is refused rather than treated as a default
one past MAX_AUTOMATION_PAGE_ITEMS, which is twenty-four here and sixty-four on the Runs lane: a page bound follows the frame arithmetic of the rows it carries
a cursor one past the largest integer this wire carries, which is a counter refusal rather than a malformed body
an empty filter admits nothing, which no listing could ever answer; it is not the same request as no filter at all
a repeat means a caller believes it asked for something it did not
an undefined state in a filter, stopped where an untyped caller reaches the builder
the envelope's fields are judged by the shared codec, whose refusal for a bound is not the one this protocol uses for a body

a grammar refusal is not a bounds refusal, and the categories differ. A space is outside the correlation identifier's grammar and inside the automation identity's, which is the difference this lane's looser identifier makes

note: Generated from the shipped Rust constructors: every canonical byte string here was produced by encoding a real message and re-read through from_canonical_bytes before it was written, and every refusal category was read back from the error Rust returned for that exact input. Counters travel as decimal strings because a JSON reader using a double would round the largest of them without saying so. Rust is the wire source of truth, so a disagreement is fixed in whichever implementation is wrong — never in this file.

requests.note: every bound at once: all three states, a cursor at the wire's integer ceiling, the largest page this protocol serves, and a correlation identifier at MAX_REQUEST_ID_BYTES. The states are recorded shuffled — the wire order is the enum's declaration order, which is neither the caller's nor alphabetical
no filter and the beginning of the listing: an explicit null, which is a different wire fact from a filter naming every state, and a cursor of zero, which is a position rather than the absence of one
a two-state filter naming exactly the two states that carry a cause

a withdrawal at the wire's ceiling revision, with an actor and a cause carrying every escape a bounded field can reach, a three-byte character and a surrogate pair; the automation identity carries a space, which this lane's grammar admits and DurableId's does not

an empty page that still reports more: an enablement filter can exclude every row in one scanned window while rows remain behind it, so a client that inferred `done` from a short page would stop early

responses.note: one automation in full, withdrawn: the actor is whoever withdrew it and the cause is why, which is the whole of the history this registry keeps. The prompt travels here and only here, with every escape a prompt can carry

a never-paused automation at revision one: the actor is the registrant rather than a resumer, and the cause is null. Registered before jobs existed, so the job columns and the prompt are null together
a stale fencing revision, which is not a rejection: the caller retries against the durable revision this carries
the identity is already registered, whatever state its row is in

rust_only_refusals.note: a withdrawn row with no stated cause: the same coupling the builder applies on the way out, met on the way in, where this surface does not hold it
an enabled row carrying a cause, which would say an automation in service was withdrawn
registration is the only writer of revision one and it always writes enabled, so a withdrawn row below revision two is a row no writer produced
the same rule on a receipt
records that do not strictly increase by durable row identity, so the next page would re-serve or skip
rows follow, with no cursor to resume from
a continuation cursor below the last row on the page, which would re-serve it
a conflict naming the revision the caller expected, which is agreement — and would tell a caller to retry with the revision it already used
a scope with no schedule to serialize under: the job columns are null together or present together, which relates two fields
an instant something is due at, on a row with nothing scheduled
a prompt on a row registered before jobs existed, which is a task nothing will ever fire — the prompt and the job imply each other
a scheduled row whose detail carries no prompt: a job that would submit nothing, refused by the same coupling the other way round

rust_only_refusals_note: Payloads the Rust constructors refuse and the generated TypeScript accepts. Each breaks a rule relating two fields of a decoded message, which the generated surface does not hold. The request-side enablement/cause coupling is deliberately absent from this list: the generated builder does apply it, and encode_refusals is where that is proved. The runner asserts these decode, so the remaining gap is measured rather than described — teaching the generator one of these rules turns the suite red until the entry moves to decode_refusals.
